key_insight: ShotStream reframes long-form video generation as streaming, next-shot synthesis conditioned only on historical context, enabling low-latency, interactive multi-shot storytelling where users can steer narratives on the fly.
problem_solved: Existing bidirectional multi-shot video models are slow and offer limited interactivity for ongoing narratives; ShotStream solves high-latency, non-interactive generation by enabling causal, on-the-fly shot synthesis that accepts dynamic user instructions.
method: Causal multi-shot architecture: generate each next shot conditioned on past shots only (no bidirectional access), enabling streaming decoding and immediate responsiveness.
Streaming prompt interface: accept and integrate user instructions mid-story so the model can alter future shots without re-generating prior frames.
Efficient on-the-fly generation techniques (lightweight temporal conditioning and incremental decoding) to reduce latency while preserving temporal coherence across shots.
impact: Allows interactive, real-time control of long-form video narratives — useful for storytelling tools, games, and live content generation — and reduces compute/latency barriers for deploying multi-shot video models in practical systems.

paper_title: ShotStream: Streaming Multi-Shot Video Generation for Interactive Storytelling
paper_authors: Yawen Luo, Xiaoyu Shi, Junhao Zhuang, Yutian Chen, Quande Liu
